python.typing: use built-in types (list[int], dict[str, T]) — no typing.List
python.errors: raise TreasuryError(ErrorCode.X, msg, field?) — never bare HTTPException except in dedicated adapters (fx.py)
python.dates: ISO 8601 strings; SQLite has no date type
python.ids: ids.new_id(prefix) — prefixes: cp, cxp, dl, hl, run, pol, adv, ...
python.docstrings: always for services and non-trivial functions; explain the invariant, not the implementation

typescript.state_refresh: after every write call `load()` in page.tsx to refetch StateResponse; never optimistic updates

comments.rule: explain WHY not WHAT — well-named identifiers do the what
comments.never: reference the current task, fix, or callers ('used by X', 'added for Y flow', 'fixes issue #123')
comments.always: reference the invariant or the surprising behaviour

commit_messages.shape: lowercase area prefix: brief change — e.g. 'hedging: sort cards by policy-gap severity'
commit_messages.never_skip_hooks: no --no-verify unless the user explicitly asks

tests.principle: seed-heavy fixtures via seed/seed.py load(); tests then read the actual book

product_language: 'Six-check gate' — the gate every path must run
'AI proposes, deterministic disposes' — the AI-vs-code pattern
'Treasury Register Connector' — first-party name for our integration surface; NEVER 'Oracle Integration Cloud' anywhere
'Bloomberg BGN composite (stubbed)' — the label for mock rate quotes
'Governance narration, not a market view' — the caveat for every AI output in FX

output_style_for_ai_prose.percentages: whole percent for coverage (60% hedged), 2dp for rates (4.25%)
output_style_for_ai_prose.priority: biggest gap first — sort explicit, never alphabetical
